 Auburn LB Xavier Atkins' status still unsettled entering LSU game
 Auburn and Alex Golesh still have not decided whether the All-American linebacker will return this week 
 Nathan King 26 In the wake of Saturday's massive upset at No. 1 Georgia, it's unclear whether Auburn will get one of its best players back for a matchup against his former team.
 Xavier Atkins' status is still undetermined, according to Alex Golesh, after the All-American linebacker did not play and did not travel with the team for the 27-24 victory in Athens over the weekend.
 "We're still working through it," Golesh said during his Monday press conference. "I don't have an update right now."
 The SEC availability report will be released Wednesday night and updated each day up until kickoff. 
 Atkins was away from the team all of last week following a suspension for undisclosed reasons by Golesh, who said those conversations would remain in-house until Atkins' status was re-evaluated after the Georgia game.
 A former LSU transfer, Atkins was a massive retention for DJ Durkin's Auburn defense in the offseason. He posted 84 tackles, 17 tackles for loss and nine sacks last season en route to All-American honors by multiple publications. This year, Atkins has 37 tackles, 7.5 tackles for loss and three sacks in only five games. 
 Without Atkins, fellow linebacker Elijah Melendez posted nine tackles, a sack, an interception and a pass breakup in the win at Georgia. Bryce Deas replaced Atkins in the starting group and had eight tackles.
 "Bryce is just a great linebacker, man," Melendez said. "He's a great athlete, great player, great dude. Like, we made a promise to each other: If we have to, we will die on this field today. We made a promise to each other to play harder than them."
 Auburn returns home this weekend to face No. 18 LSU (11 a.m. CT, ABC).
